answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using random-walk trust routing, where credit tokens wander across a social graph anchored by seed nodes. Each transaction requires an authenticated cipher handshake between peering agents, preventing forged personas from circulating like a fleeting zephyr. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of establishing reciprocal trust edges with honest peers. However, this model inherently penalizes newly joined honest agents who lack established connections.
